nodes.AttackPattern: A CAPEC attack pattern (CAPEC-ID) describing an adversarial technique at an abstract level.
nodes.Category: A grouping of related attack patterns sharing a common attribute or theme.
nodes.View: A curated subset or perspective over the CAPEC catalog (e.g., WASC, OWASP).
nodes.Weakness: A CWE software weakness exploited by one or more attack patterns.
nodes.TaxonomyEntry: A mapping between a CAPEC attack pattern and an external taxonomy (e.g., ATT&CK, WASC).
nodes.ExternalReference: A published resource (paper, CVE, URL) referenced by a CAPEC entry.
nodes.ExecutionStep: A discrete numbered step in an attack pattern's execution flow.
nodes.Skill: A required attacker capability (e.g., low/medium/high skill level) for executing an attack pattern.
nodes.Consequence: A security impact or outcome that results from a successful attack pattern.
nodes.Mitigation: A countermeasure or defensive recommendation for an attack pattern.

relationships.ChildOf: An AttackPattern is a more specific variant of a parent AttackPattern.
relationships.ParentOf: An AttackPattern is the parent of a more specific child AttackPattern.
relationships.CanPrecede: An AttackPattern can occur before another in an attack chain.
relationships.CanFollow: An AttackPattern can occur after another in an attack chain.
relationships.PeerOf: Two AttackPatterns are related alternatives at the same abstraction level.
relationships.CanAlsoBe: An AttackPattern can also be characterized as another AttackPattern.
relationships.EXPLOITS_WEAKNESS: An AttackPattern exploits a specific CWE Weakness.
relationships.MAPS_TO: An AttackPattern maps to an entry in an external taxonomy (TaxonomyEntry).
relationships.MEMBER_OF: An AttackPattern is a member of a Category.
relationships.IN_VIEW: An AttackPattern or Category appears in a View.
relationships.HAS_EXECUTION_STEP: An AttackPattern contains an ordered ExecutionStep.
relationships.NEXT_STEP: One ExecutionStep is followed by another in sequence.
relationships.REQUIRES_SKILL: An AttackPattern requires an attacker to possess a Skill.
relationships.HAS_CONSEQUENCE: An AttackPattern leads to a Consequence if successful.
relationships.HAS_MITIGATION: An AttackPattern is addressed by a Mitigation.
relationships.HAS_REFERENCE: An AttackPattern, Category, or View is documented by an ExternalReference.
